scope: Evidence-driven closure for the 38 affected-system obligations; formal closure is separate from economic acceptance.

assumptions.statement: Defined GHC Double values use IEEE binary64, without unsafe capability forgery; excludes bottom and compiler/hardware bugs.
Trusted callers provide truthful evidence; no research proposal is imported into an order-authorizing path.
Z3, the checker, compiler, runtimes and hardware belong to the trusted computing base; no independently checked proof certificate.
Two callers and atomic abstract steps; completion fairness for draining; no production refinement.
Integer indexing is exact; historical publication and first-seen timing are not independently witnessed.
Exact real algebra does not establish binary64 accounting, market fills or calibrated costs.
Return and total-debit bounds in sufficient-condition lemmas are environmental hypotheses, not established crypto-market facts. Pre-bar drifted exposure differs from a proposed target.

Ordinary fixed-shape base NumPy numeric arrays, unchanged primitive bindings and no concurrent writes; audited metadata helper ASTs and restricted AST interpreter/NumPy argument-only dependency semantics are trusted. No publication-time, caller symbol selection, runtime/compiler or universal observation refinement proof.

Checked fold setup is entered with admitted ordinary fixed-shape numeric arrays and stable symbol/split bindings. Python slicing/range/RNG, NumPy reductions, Scale constructor snapshots and the restricted AST checker are trusted; no hostile subclasses, aliases or concurrent writers. Whole-panel admission and full Replay/compiler refinement remain unproved.

Ordinary Path/bytes and JSON built-ins, stable globals and externally supplied expected metadata; no concurrent mutation, hostile subclass or monkeypatch. Python control flow, JSON/hashlib/NumPy, validators and Network constructor are trusted. The audited AST checker is not a verified interpreter; finite atomic gates do not prove helper internals or cryptographic authenticity.

Ordinary stable Replay fields; integer indices and binary64 reward/equity/units, native identity/comparison behavior, stable arrays/helpers, no concurrent mutation or hostile subclasses. The restricted AST translator, Python control flow, _finite_real and successor representation/shape/finiteness predicates are trusted. Admission conditions do not prove cash-flow completeness, fill realism, helper internals or full Replay/compiler refinement.

Correctly shaped float64 arrays and Boolean done masks, matching rows, stable primitive bindings and no concurrent mutation. Trusted AST checker and vector-to-scalar correspondence with separate IEEE binary64 RNE operations, not fused reassociation or full interpreter refinement. The finite-product theorem requires finite next value AND later carry; finite network outputs do not ensure finite carry. Batch normalization is outside the noninterference claim.

Native immutable tuples, native float/bool inputs, stable bindings, separate IEEE binary64 RNE and trusted math.isfinite/Python primitives; source skeleton/scalarization/model abstraction, compiler and solver are trusted. Normal resource availability and terminating primitives; no concurrent monkey patching. No whole-interpreter refinement, normalized-advantage guarantee, nonterminal roundoff bound or full learner correction.

Ordinary correctly shaped float64 arrays and in-range actions with positive behavior probabilities, stable bindings and no mutation; source scalarization, softmax/simplex and vector correspondence, separate RNE primitives, analytic softmax derivative identity and compiler/solver semantics are trusted. Exact-real claims are not full binary64, NumPy, neural-network or optimizer refinement.

Ordinary aligned float64 arrays and in-range actions, stable bindings and no mutation; trusted NumPy first-argmax/vector-to-scalar semantics, softmax and logarithm/derivative identities, prescribed transcendental intermediates, separate IEEE binary64 RNE, Python/compiler/solver and AST translator. No full training-loop or runtime refinement, policy lower-bound theorem, end-to-end witness reachability or historical prevalence.

Trusted exact source skeleton, AST translator, Python/NumPy/runtime and ordinary base arrays; helpers do not mutate shared inputs, primitive operations terminate, one writer, and final stores succeed uninterrupted for the narrow theorem. No full runtime refinement, multi-writer safety or unassisted thread-race evidence. The real clipping norm premise is not proved for rounded NumPy reductions; no Adam step-size, convergence or economic guarantee. Instrumentation observes and injects an exception deliberately; no historical occurrence is claimed. Stronger atomicity remains a blocker. Python documents that exceptions escaping opcode traces may cause undefined interpreter behavior; injected interruption is a pinned-runtime diagnostic, not a portable implementation theorem. Normal-store observation does not require raising an exception.

Trusted AST/model translation, ordinary base numeric arrays, stable bindings/constants and NumPy finite/first-argmax semantics; no full runtime or neural-policy refinement. Predicate, clock and BaseException failures are not caught by the forward Exception handler. The elapsed proof starts from the final scalar, not clock conversion or authenticity; measured time excludes later output validation and selection. Nonreturning forward has no preemption; proposal is not an authorized order. No staleness, uncertainty, policy quality, economic value or actual deadline guarantee.

Trusted AST translation, admitted base arrays, stable bindings and NumPy cumprod, reduction and broadcast semantics; no full runtime refinement. Exact-real algebra does not establish binary64 accuracy, unbiasedness, behavior support, confidence coverage or statistical reliability. DR additionally assumes q_t=v_t pathwise; equal policies alone are insufficient. CE-RL-018 is a general-helper witness and is outside the current deterministic six-step short-OPE weight domain. Underflow-raise callers get ValueError. No original OPE rerun or market prevalence claim.

Trusted Python 3.13.3 native-type/isfinite checks, exact float-to-Fraction conversion and integer/rational primitives, AST translation and solver; stable bindings and normal resources. Ghost processed-count maps the source loop to the model; base/step SMT lemmas are not full interpreter or Fraction refinement. Model liveness assumes terminating primitives. No allocation-recovery, physical deadline, upstream weight-underflow recovery, statistical effective-sample-size or behavior-support guarantee. Diagnostic remains disconnected from frozen OPE/training and production; no policy result is repaired or promoted.

Trusted Python/NumPy primitives, left-insertion search semantics, exact regular integer grids and stable ordinary source bindings; AST source binding/extraction is not full interpreter refinement. Hashes identify bytes, not publication timing, source truth or historical prevalence. No arbitrary-registration/CSV-schema, cash-realism or universal floating-point theorem.

Stable ordinary Replay state; returning and exception-free shield/observation/market/_trade/_risk primitives until the final reward check; Python control flow, AST translation and source-to-model abstraction trusted. Ghost admission/check tags record abstract ordering only. Helper attempts are not guaranteed fills. No numeric accounting, full runtime refinement, concurrency, physical deadline or production lifecycle proof.

The cutoff applies only to the pinned ordering abstraction. Stable ordinary dataclass attributes, standard replacement semantics, source/AST interpretation and all earlier A-REPLAY-ORDER helper assumptions are trusted. Actual time-to-end observations, numeric rewards, risk outcomes and policy actions can differ with remaining length. The integer branch lemma and finite lift checks are not universal interpreter refinement or an observation/reward bisimulation.

Exact-real arithmetic with positive starting/intermediate wealth for the product induction; complete source row publication, stable ordinary state, returning helpers and trusted Python/NumPy/AST semantics. Costs are nonnegative supplied vectors; fill quantities, fee formation and impact square roots are not proved. Real identities and synthetic tolerance tests do not establish universal binary64 error bounds, finite outputs, runtime refinement or economic superiority.

Trusted ordinary Python AST/identity/short-circuit execution, GHC constructors and guard order, defined arguments, returning monotonic clock; no runtime patching or compiler corruption. Explicit research command invocation opts into simulation; no production candidate integration exists.

The validator proves neither this implication nor the substance of empirical acceptance evidence; it checks consistency, reproduction and hashes. Scope or sufficiency changes require review.

Trust pinned GHC 9.4.8, bundled Cabal 3.8.1.0 parsing/linking/type semantics, Aeson generic required fields, ordinary Python Network/base numeric arrays, NumPy primitives and clock reads. No runtime monkeypatching, custom ndarray dispatch, injected code/mounts, replaced packages/binaries/PATH, manual artifact conversion or administrative invocation of training from production. Reviewed runtime recipes/helpers are unchanged, not a proof of deployed images. Existing champion learning and live authority are outside this delivered-research isolation claim.

Ordinary pinned GIL-enabled CPython 3.13.3 slotted reference reads/stores and lock primitives are atomic; stable base NumPy 2.3.5 arrays, finite scans and byte serialization preserve values; frozen dataclass/native bytes discipline is respected. Stable caller buffers during copies, normal resources, no malicious reflection, custom dispatch or monkeypatching. No compiler/runtime refinement theorem, wall-clock preemption or durable transaction is established; interrupted lock handoff may strand writers but cannot expose a mixed snapshot.

Trusted pinned GHC 9.4.8/process 1.6.18.0/unix 2.7.3/bytestring 0.11.5.3 bounded buffer/IO primitives and self executable; stable PID until this sole parent reaps; no descendants, external reaper, hostile replacement or injected code. Monotonic clock, bounded process creation/IO/signal primitives and parent/timer scheduling. Repeated async cancellation, process death, neural arithmetic equivalence and production shutdown are not proved. See inference-process-v2-contract.md.

GHC Integer/Int, monotonic clock, System.Timeout and compiler semantics are trusted. Clock does not wrap during one shutdown; bounded scheduler, clock and logging service is needed for wall-time interpretation. Source scalarization and finite atomic-stage abstraction are trusted, not full IO refinement. Child cancellation need not terminate an uninterruptible action.

Pinned GHC 9.4.8/base 4.17.2.1 MVar, masking, forkIOWithUnmask, finally and System.Timeout semantics; finite registry, available memory, private completion cells and bounded scheduler/primitive progress. Completion covers tracked callback/finalizers only. Atomic-step interpretation and source-to-model correspondence are reviewed and tested, not fully proved IO refinement. Closure begins at registry lock, not HTTP beginDrain.

Pinned GHC/base mask, forkIOWithUnmask, MVar and atomic IORef semantics; private counters/gates, finite allocation, total nonthrowing counter predicates, failing fork creates no child, and masked atomic exception-safe publication. Actual Main publication uses modifyMVar_ and pure HM.insert. Release has no blocking lock wait. Eventual release requires callback completion/cancellation and scheduler progress; no full IO refinement, durable recovery or HTTP drain guarantee. Current pool counter operations use STM under A-DRAIN-POOL; IORef wording describes the preserved baseline. The original standalone conformance uses an independent open drain controller.

Current pool counter operations use STM under A-DRAIN-POOL; IORef wording describes the preserved baseline. The original standalone conformance uses an independent open drain controller.

Current pool counter operations use STM under A-DRAIN-POOL; IORef wording describes the preserved baseline. The original standalone conformance uses an independent open drain controller.

Drain latch and counters are private; reservation STM contains finite pure computation, no retry, IO or callback. Contention/scheduler service and callback cooperation remain assumptions, not hard deadlines. Pre-drain owners may execute after drain; no whole-server bot/order authorization, durable recovery or complete IO refinement.

Pinned Python AST/control flow/argument binding, pandas equality filtering and conversion, NumPy immutable bytes views and argument-only numeric primitives, SHA-256 collision resistance and the reviewed source checker are trusted. Ordinary registered files/base arrays, stable bindings, no hostile subclasses, runtime patching, arbitrary injected callbacks or concurrent writers. Full interpreter/library refinement, publication witnesses and online admission causality are not proved. Shared training transforms/policies are explicitly permitted global inputs.

Expected identity is a caller trust anchor, not a truth/authenticity theorem. Reviewed source-to-primitive correspondence and equality-class abstraction are assumptions, supplemented by actual-code conformance, not whole-interpreter refinement. Torn/replaced files are allowed: only the returned read bytes are compared. No OS sandbox, crash-atomic persistence, provenance authenticity or whole-production authorization theorem.

Fork returns a thread or fails without one; private gate release and uncontended final cell replacement complete under masking. WHNF is not deep evaluation. Returning primitives and weakly fair lock/thread scheduling support protocol progress, not a wall-clock bound. Reviewed source/model correspondence is not whole-GHC IO refinement. External stop/removal, already-started action failures, persistent/cross-instance ownership, inventory freshness, drain linearization, resource exhaustion and durable recovery remain unresolved.

Pinned CPython 3.13.3/pathlib/io and filesystem exclusive-create semantics; ordinary built-in objects and registered scalar identifiers, fixed reviewed code and trusted dependency/helper effects. Parent-directory and open-object identities are stable; leaf insertion and collisions before open are explicitly modeled. No malicious parent replacement, privileged filesystem mutation, external champion deletion/recreation, code injection or manual adoption of unfinished output. Source/model correspondence is reviewed and conformance-tested, not whole-language/kernel refinement. No crash durability, whole-archive atomicity, deployed-image or inherited production selection-correctness guarantee.

A-SHIELD-COMPOSITION: pinned Python3.13.3/NumPy2.3.5 ordinary objects, sequential control flow, fresh object identity, array-copy and reviewed primitive effects; fixed registered callbacks and complete source inventory. No hostile monkeypatching/subclasses, reflective caller mutation, asynchronous injected callbacks or direct external private-helper invocation. Local receiver ownership is source-checked, not merely assumed. Reviewed effect/source-model correspondence is not whole-language refinement. Numeric solvency, all hard constraints, truthful evidence/provider timing, asynchronous revocation, crash recovery, inherited production races and deployed images remain uncertified.

A-PIT-WITNESS: caller timestamp/revision evidence is truthful and clock-consistent; authenticity and historical availability are not proved. Exact CPython integer, tuple, frozen dataclass and NumPy copying semantics, ordinary base objects and trusted reviewed primitive effects. No hostile reflection/monkeypatching or concurrent source mutation. Source/model mapping is reviewed and conformance-tested, not compiler refinement. Per-bar decision vintages are frozen, not retrospective rolling revisions. Frozen CSV, actual market fills, numerical accounting, production ingestion and empirical superiority remain outside this certificate.

A-OPE-RATIONAL: exact CPython Fraction/integer, finite base-float conversion, tuple and frozen dataclass semantics; unchanged reviewed bindings, no hostile reflection or concurrent source mutation. Caller supplies authentic complete causal trajectories and true logged propensities; arithmetic admission does not establish support, value-model validity or statistical reliability. Source/model mapping is reviewed and conformance-tested, not whole-language refinement. Bit caps bound individual arithmetic objects, not wall time or process memory. Frozen v1 OPE, replay, funding, Q/CQL and general BLAS numeric behavior remain outside these certificates.

A-BUNDLE-FS: trusted pinned CPython byte/JSON/descriptor semantics and local POSIX exclusive open/link, no-follow regular-file checks and fsync honored by filesystem/device. Stable caller-selected existing directory, no hostile namespace/content mutation or forged admitted source evidence. Finitely many crashes, eventual healthy IO, adequate space and fair scheduling for progress. Process-kill tests do not test hardware power failure. Orphan staging files may remain and are never adopted or automatically scavenged. Model correspondence is reviewed source extraction plus actual conformance, not kernel/compiler refinement. Training archive recovery, inherited bot recovery, whole-system progress and production authorization remain outside scope.

The reviewed eligibility projection distinguishes research computation from promotion eligibility. Ordinary pinned Python/GHC/JSON primitives, fixed source/callbacks and existing A-PROMOTION-BOUNDARY/A-CAPABILITY-BUILD conditions are trusted; source constructors, rejecting predicates and effect exclusion establish stage preservation rather than assuming it. No injected code, replacement binaries or manual artifact conversion. No future promotion service, liveness, production authority or whole-runtime refinement is certified.

Ordinary GHC9.4.8/base4.17.2.1/stm2.5.1.0/containers primitives, serializable STM rollback, exact Integer and Seq append/view/filter semantics, private cells, defined values, finite allocation, terminating callbacks/cleanup and weak scheduler fairness for continuously enabled actions. No fairness is assumed for intermittent admission; no wall-clock bound, overload guarantee, whole-server IO/compiler refinement or persistent recovery theorem.

Pinned CPython3.13.3 Fraction/int/isqrt/dataclass semantics, ordinary immutable native values and stable bindings, Z3 and reviewed AST translation, GHC9.4.8 Rational oracle, sufficient resources and truthful complete per-bar funding inputs. Integer size bounds are not allocation recovery or physical timing guarantees. No binary64 conversion, whole-interpreter refinement, realistic fills or causal data provenance is established.

Pinned CPython3.13.3 re/int/Fraction/dataclass semantics, ordinary immutable native values and stable bindings, Z3 and reviewed AST translation, GHC9.4.8 Rational oracle and sufficient resources. Bit bounds are not allocation recovery or physical timing guarantees. The canonical decimal domain is a numeric admission contract, not evidence that any provider emits it or that a record is causally available. Endpoint lemmas are quantifier-free over unbounded integers and use explicit sortedness instances rather than a quantified grid axiom; the exhaustive sweep check covers only the registered small grid. The frozen development loader and CE-RL-019 there remain unchanged and refuted; runner/learner composition, actual release/first-seen timing, revisions, symbol scoping and original38 remain unresolved.

Inherits A-REPLAY-ACCOUNT-V2 and A-FUNDING-EVENTS-V2. Treats a settlement's grid time as its availability time; this is an assumption, not a provider release or first-seen proof. Replays a fixed caller-supplied target schedule: no policy, observation causality, learning, OPE, shield precedence or economic claim follows. Index and telescoping lemmas are over unbounded integers and exact reals with explicit per-step premises; the finite model abstracts numeric values and covers horizons 1..8; metamorphic and oracle checks are seeded tests, not proofs. Frozen sequential_replay_v1, its loader and original38 remain unresolved.

Pinned CPython3.13.3 float/math exp, log and fsum semantics on IEEE binary64 RNE hardware; primitive bounds 0 <= exp(x) <= 1 for x <= 0 and 0 <= log(s) <= 2 for 1 <= s <= 3; A-FP-ROUNDING (each basic operation returns the rounding of its exact real result) and the standard model |fl(x)-x| <= 2^-53|x|, neither machine-proved for the CPython build. Full binary64 bit-blasting returned unknown within 120 s, so the binary64 shift claim rests on the named rounding assumption; the bitwise draft claim was refuted by CE-RL-024 and resolved by zero canonicalization. The kernel is disconnected: frozen bellman_gradient/train_q, F-RL-Q-FINITE and F-RL-CQL-SHIFT stay refuted and unchanged; no learner composition, convergence, conservative-value guarantee, support or economic claim follows; original38 remain unresolved.

Each IEEE binary64 basic operation (add, subtract, multiply, divide) in the pinned CPython build returns the round-to-nearest-even rounding of its exact real result, with signed-zero results as specified by IEEE 754; not machine-proved for the interpreter, compiler or hardware.

Owner-approved standard purge/embargo definition (2026-10-06): embargo constrains only training rows after a fold's test window and is vacuous for these forward folds; the six-bar gap is not two additive regions. Access means label/outcome reads; observation lookback is governed by causality obligations 1 and 17. short_ope's whole-series finiteness admission reads all values but its outcome is constant on the hash-fixed panel. Trusts the Python interpreter, NumPy slicing/indexing and rng.integers upper-exclusive semantics, AST translation and Z3. Production ingestion is outside the scope.

Executable synthetic witness and seeded fixed-scale probe on unchanged source; trusts the Python interpreter, NumPy and the AST binding. The refutation concerns training-time observations of the frozen screen; evaluation observations use a scale fitted strictly before testStart. No historical prevalence or economic effect is established. Frozen code is not edited; a causal-scale successor needs a new registration.

A-GAP-BOUND: per-bar |return| <= 1/2, |funding per unit| <= 3/100 of the prior price, finite positive prices and finite funding held in binary64 (float64) arrays as the delivered loader builds them (other dtypes admitted by Replay are outside the certificate), prices and equity in [2^-400, 2^400] so every product and quotient, including e/p on the missed-fill branch, stays below 2^1000 (no overflow), execution within the registered stress maxima, monotone numpy.sqrt on [0,1], and the binary64 standard rounding model. This is an assumption about market data, not a fact; paths outside it can breach any bound (CE-RL-002/003 stay refuted). Proposal rejections end episodes without an order and leave the last in-bounds position unliquidated by design. Production order sizing and rounding belong to obligation 9 and are not claimed.

Per-row reconciliation reading: each recorded debit against its stated formula on the executed binary64 inputs and the recorded wealth roll-forward; bars with invalid market data reject. Premises: A-GAP-BOUND's market limits (per-bar |p1/p0 - 1| <= 1/2 and |funding per unit| <= 3/100 of the prior price), its range premise (prices and equity in [2^-400, 2^400]), its execution maxima (cost multiplier <= 5/2, impact_bps <= 10, funding multiplier <= 2, as bound to the runner's registered stresses by F-RL-BOUNDS-SOURCE; Execution itself accepts larger values, which are outside the certificate) and binary64 arrays from the delivered loader (so cost terms are np.float64 scalars and CPython's sum() uses left-to-right addition, not its exact-float compensated path; checked per debit), A-FP-ROUNDING with |fl(x)-x| <= u|x| + H, correctly rounded numpy.sqrt. Fill calibration against real venues is empirical and belongs to the economic gate; it is not claimed. Global trajectory error growth is not bounded; reconciliation is per row.

Source certificate over haskell/app import lists; the compiler is trusted to reject any capture combinator that is not imported, and library code (http-client, warp, postgresql-simple) is trusted not to swallow asynchronous exceptions it does not own. GHC semantics are trusted: killThread returns after delivery and SomeAsyncException covers ThreadKilled, Timeout and UserInterrupt. Stop completes only after delivery to masked regions. This removes post-stop exchange actions of a killed worker; it does not prove persistent owner-row linearization, account identity or cross-instance uniqueness, which keep obligation 15 open.

Non-trading servers carry their checked-in role label (Fly read-only, Fly research, Hetzner research via the managed env overlay, all bound by F-LIVE-ROLE-GATE-SOURCE); no out-of-band live actor uses the same exchange account; GHC asynchronous-exception and MVar semantics and the Binance account endpoint's uid field are trusted; an exchange request already sent before a stop or refusal is not recalled; concurrent manual trades on one account are one owner (the operator).

In-process readiness of one trading server. Venue snapshots are assumed complete and truthful when read; exchange-side changes outside the system (stop or liquidation fills, the exchange UI) between scans are bounded only by the freshness window. Ownership reconciliation relies on obligation 15's certificates. Readiness is reported, not enforced: it gates no order path, and /health always returns status ok. Readiness reports the auto-start account (the server credentials the live bot fleet trades with): the scan reconciles that account's venue inventory against the auto-start tenant's runtime, so a bot on the same account under another tenant keeps readiness false rather than true. Other users' accounts in multi-user mode are not covered by /ready.

Exchange symbol filters and token decimals are taken as truthful; real-number cap reasoning over the reviewed sizing source with binary64 comparisons as the code performs them. Exposure caps are maxOrderQuote, available balance and the venue limits the code checks; the optional market-risk gate is separate.

One server process; CLI modes reached only from main run as separate processes and are not drained. Work admitted before the drain latch (pre-drain owners) may complete, including a bot order routine's protection orders. Running bots make no new order decisions while draining; their positions carry over to adoption after restart. Background persistence (state sync, listen-key and ops cleanup) is shutdown reconciliation. Credential probes remain available while draining. STM/IORef latch semantics are trusted.

System-initiated retries: transport, timestamp, bot re-decisions on later candles, retried bot starts and keyed manual trades. A client re-submitting an unkeyed manual trade issues a new intent. The venue's position and balance reads are assumed to reflect an applied order before the next decision (read-after-write). DEX swaps are manual and never retried by the system.

Truthful completed-bar availability including processing lag and caller-aligned funding buckets; native immutable objects and trusted CPython Fraction/dataclass plus checked replay-accounting-v2 primitives; sufficient resources, no hostile reflection or monkeypatching. Source/SMT/model composition is reviewed and conformance-tested, not interpreter/compiler refinement. No authentic historical releases, calibrated fills, learning, OPE or economic claim.

entries.claim: Every definition that mutates the bot runtime map (start publication, start-failure removal, Starting-to-Running promotion, stop, worker cleanup) and every possibly-live manual trade completion bumps the runtime epoch inside the same runtime lock; the readiness scan revokes readiness, reads its runtime snapshot together with the epoch under the lock, and publishes readiness tagged with that epoch and scan time only when the scan reconciled; both HTTP readers (/ready and /health) report ready only when the tagged epoch is current and the scan is within the freshness bound. A possibly-live manual trade is counted in flight from admission to completion under the runtime lock, bumping the epoch at both ends, the scan reads the in-flight count with its snapshot and never publishes readiness while a trade is in flight, and readers read the in-flight count before the epoch (barrier reads) and require it to be zero.

entries.limitations: In-process readiness of one trading server. Venue snapshots are assumed complete and truthful when read; exchange-side changes outside the system (stop or liquidation fills, the exchange UI) between scans are bounded only by the freshness window. Ownership reconciliation relies on obligation 15's certificates. Readiness is reported, not enforced: it gates no order path, and /health always returns status ok. Readiness reports the auto-start account (the server credentials the live bot fleet trades with): the scan reconciles that account's venue inventory against the auto-start tenant's runtime, so a bot on the same account under another tenant keeps readiness false rather than true. Other users' accounts in multi-user mode are not covered by /ready.

entries.limitations: Pinned CPython3.13.3 float/math exp, log and fsum semantics on IEEE binary64 RNE hardware; primitive bounds 0 <= exp(x) <= 1 for x <= 0 and 0 <= log(s) <= 2 for 1 <= s <= 3; A-FP-ROUNDING (each basic operation returns the rounding of its exact real result) and the standard model |fl(x)-x| <= 2^-53|x|, neither machine-proved for the CPython build. The kernel is disconnected: frozen bellman_gradient/train_q, F-RL-Q-FINITE and F-RL-CQL-SHIFT stay refuted and unchanged; no learner composition, convergence, conservative-value guarantee, support or economic claim follows; original38 remain unresolved.

entries.claim: No module under haskell/app can capture an asynchronous exception except through reviewed forwarding threads: every exception-capturing combinator (try, catch, handle and their variants from Control.Exception, Control.Monad.Catch, UnliftIO or GHC.IO) is imported only by Trader.App.AsyncSafe and the async-filtering BacktestGate, all imports of those modules are explicit and unqualified, and trySync/catchSync rethrow every SomeAsyncException; so a killed bot worker, a timed-out call or a stopped heartbeat cannot convert the kill into an ordinary error and keep acting.

entries.limitations: Source certificate over haskell/app import lists; the compiler is trusted to reject any capture combinator that is not imported, and library code (http-client, warp, postgresql-simple) is trusted not to swallow asynchronous exceptions it does not own. GHC semantics are trusted: killThread returns after delivery and SomeAsyncException covers ThreadKilled, Timeout and UserInterrupt. Stop completes only after delivery to masked regions. This removes post-stop exchange actions of a killed worker; it does not prove persistent owner-row linearization, account identity or cross-instance uniqueness, which keep obligation 15 open.
